facts.raw_span: A 67-year-old man
hypertension, dyslipidaemia, stage 3 chronic kidney disease, active smoking (35 pack-years), a family history of ischaemic heart disease
prior percutaneous coronary interventions (2008, 2017, 2022) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina
exercise stress test induced angina at 50 W without ECG changes
normal sinus rhythm, Q waves in lead III, and biphasic T waves in leads III and aVF
left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities
patent stents in the circumflex artery, non-significant disease in the left anterior descending artery, and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis
ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3
subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch
recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
new QTc prolongation to 500 ms

support_spans: patent stents in the circumflex artery, non-significant disease in the left anterior descending artery, and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis
ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3
subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch
concepts.why: The patient presented with angina and had significant coronary artery stenosis, ST-segment elevation, and subocclusion of a coronary branch, all of which are indicative of acute coronary syndrome.

support_spans: recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
new QTc prolongation to 500 ms
akinesia of all apical segments, later extending to mid-segments, hyperkinesia of the basal segments, and severely reduced LVEF of 35%
concepts.why: The patient developed ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, and QTc prolongation, and had a significantly reduced LVEF with apical akinesia, all of which are characteristic of takotsubo syndrome.

support_spans: prior percutaneous coronary interventions (2008, 2017, 2022) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3
concepts.why: The patient had a history of myocardial infarction and presented with ST-segment elevation, which is indicative of myocardial infarction.
It explains the uncovered finding of left ventricular ejection fraction of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities, which is a characteristic feature of stress cardiomyopathy.

rationales.F03: Prior percutaneous coronary interventions suggest a history of coronary artery disease, increasing the likelihood of Acute Coronary Syndrome and Myocardial Infarction.
rationales.F08: Patent stents and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis indicate coronary artery disease, supporting Acute Coronary Syndrome and Myocardial Infarction.
rationales.F09: ST-segment elevation is a key indicator of Myocardial Infarction, but in this context, it also supports Acute Coronary Syndrome, while making Takotsubo Syndrome less likely due to the presence of coronary artery disease.
rationales.F11: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation can occur in both Acute Coronary Syndrome and Takotsubo Syndrome, but the presence of coronary artery disease makes Acute Coronary Syndrome more likely.
rationales.F12: New QTc prolongation can be seen in various cardiac conditions, including Takotsubo Syndrome, making it a moderate indicator for this condition.

frontier_selector.why: The evidence of akinesia of all apical segments, later extending to mid-segments, hyperkinesia of the basal segments, and severely reduced LVEF of 35% decided it.
